To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
over-sampling is the preferred method to balance imbalanced data sets, especially when the data are highly imbalanced.

(i) the performance of the preprocessing methods is not affected by the classifier used; (ii) the preprocessing methods are more effective when dealing with imbalanced databases; and (iii) under-sampling is more effective than over-sampling when the data set is not imbalanced.
over-sampling outperforms under sampling when data sets are highly imbalanced, whereas both strategies are equivalent in the case of low imbalances.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following question: what is the effect of preprocessing on learning?
the problem of learning in the presence of imbalanced data sets, which is a common situation in real-world applications.
the following questions: • How do the resampling algorithms affect the performance of the classifiers when the imbalance ratio of the data set is low, moderate or high?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, when dealing with imbalanced data, it is better to over-sample the minority class, especially when dealing with very imbalanced data sets, since it consistently outperforms all the other strategies.
the effectiveness of the preprocessing methods depends on the level of class imbalance of the data set, and that this effectiveness does not change when different classifiers are used.

(1) the effectiveness of preprocessing is strongly dependent on the imbalance ratio, (2) the effectiveness of the preprocessing methods is strongly related to the classifier, (3) the effectiveness of under-sampling the minority classes and over-sampling the majority classes is strongly related to both the classifier and the imbalance ratio.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the performance of a classifier on an imbalanced data set depends mainly on the imbalance ratio, whereas the resampling strategy has a very poor effect.
the performance of the preprocessing methods depends on both the classifier and the class distribution.
(i) over-sampling is the best strategy for strongly imbalanced data sets; and (ii) the classifier has a poor influence on the performance of the resampling methods.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, when dealing with imbalanced data, the choice of the resampling strategy should depend on the imbalance ratio of the data set.
the choice of the resampling strategy is more important for the final performance than the choice of the classifier.
the effectiveness of the preprocessing methods when dealing to different levels of class imbalances depends on the imbalance ratio and not on the classifier used.
